subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this four-layer collaboration stack in core, split it into narrower core/plugin API tracks, or keep the broad stack out of core while tracking only narrow primitives like #42475 and #65403?
rationale: Automation cannot choose this direction because it changes product architecture, config/defaults, persistent memory/session state, security boundaries, provider cost admission, and plugin/core ownership.

options.title: Split into narrow tracks
options.body: Keep #35203 as umbrella design input while separately reviewing budget enforcement, agent meetings, capability indexing, and memory-visibility APIs.

options.title: Approve a core stack
options.body: Sponsor the full collaboration architecture in core with explicit schema, storage, upgrade, security, and operator UX plans before implementation.

options.title: Defer broad stack outside core
options.body: Route optional collaboration behavior to plugins or external experiments and extend core APIs only when blockers are proven.

recommendation.title: Split into narrow tracks
recommendation.body: Keep #35203 as umbrella design input while separately reviewing budget enforcement, agent meetings, capability indexing, and memory-visibility APIs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed link to the current subagent/config surfaces and the adjacent scoped capability-profile foundation.
